questions.q: For Fabric items OTHER than Power BI, at what granularity does Purview capture lineage by default?
options: Item level only (e.g., a Lakehouse as a whole, not its individual tables)
Workspace level only, with no item detail at all
questions.explain: Non-Power BI Fabric items get item-level lineage. Sub-item metadata scanning for Lakehouse tables/files is in preview, but sub-item lineage still isn't supported.

questions.q: What is the Power BI lineage artifact chain, in order, per the lesson?
questions.explain: Purview captures Power BI lineage in the sequence Dataflow to Dataset to Report to Dashboard.

questions.q: Column-level (subartifact) lineage inside a Power BI dataset is currently supported only when the dataset's source is which of these?
questions.explain: Subartifact (column/measure-level) lineage and transformation details are only supported when the Power BI dataset's source is Azure SQL Database.

questions.q: What happens to lineage capture when a Power BI query uses a dynamic M query parameter (e.g., passing a server name as a parameter)?
options: Lineage isn't captured for that connection at all
Lineage is captured with extra detail
Lineage is captured but delayed by 24 hours
Purview throws a visible configuration error
questions.explain: Dynamic M query parameters prevent Purview from capturing lineage for that connection — a known limitation to watch for.

questions.q: Which four source types currently support lineage between Power BI artifacts and external data assets?
options: Azure SQL Database, Azure Blob Storage, Azure Data Lake Storage Gen1, and Gen2
Any source Power BI can connect to
questions.explain: External lineage for Power BI artifacts is currently limited to Azure SQL Database, Azure Blob Storage, Azure Data Lake Storage Gen1, and Gen2.
